subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should `message:sending` internal hooks be a post-policy, observation-only notification of messages that will actually send, with underscore spelling normalized once at registration?
rationale: The current patch implicitly defines a compatibility and security-sensitive hook contract; source and tests cannot decide whether maintainers intend internal hooks to observe pre-policy content or how broadly underscore aliases should apply.

options.title: Post-policy notification
options.body: Emit once after typed rewriting/cancellation, normalize the documented HOOK.md spelling at registration, and move heartbeat behavior to a separate PR.

options.title: Pre-policy observer
options.body: Keep pre-policy delivery but explicitly document that trusted internal hooks may see content later rewritten or canceled, define alias duplication semantics, and require live security-oriented proof.

options.title: Pause for unified hooks
options.body: Defer this bridge until a broader internal/typed hook unification establishes one canonical event and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Post-policy notification
recommendation.body: Emit once after typed rewriting/cancellation, normalize the documented HOOK.md spelling at registration, and move heartbeat behavior to a separate PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active exactly-once message-sending work most directly owns the relevant delivery boundary and channel interactions.
